To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the amygdala is involved in the acquisition and extinction of conditioned fear and (2) the strength of the circuitry connecting the amygdala to the prefrontal cortex is crucial for efficient emotional regulation.

(1) the strength of the circuitry connecting the amygdala with the mPFC is related to the capacity for emotional regulation, (2) the strength of amygdala-mPCFC circuitry is related to the ability to extinguish fear, and (3) these relationships are compromised in normal anxiety and even more so in pathological anxiety.
the strength of the functional connectivity of the mPFC-amygdala circuit is a key determinant of successful extinction learning and is related to the capacity for emotional regulation.

understanding the mechanisms of emotional regulation in normal and pathological states of anxiety.
understanding the role of the human amygdala and its interactions with other brain structures in the generation and modulation of emotion and anxiety.
the neural circuitry that supports the ability of humans to regulate the emotional response to aversive events.

the strength of amygdala-mPFc connectivity is a crucial determinant of anxiety.
